name: 理解目标
scenario: the project objective
focus: Clarifying the goal before starting work
chunks: Before I start, I want to make sure I understand what success looks like.
The outcome we are aiming for is a working prototype by the end of the month.
Could you clarify how this fits into the larger project timeline?
Let me summarise the goal to make sure we are aligned.
patterns: The outcome we are aiming for is ___.
Could you clarify how ___?
dialogue: Lin, here is the project brief. Do you have any questions before you start?
Before I start, I want to make sure I understand what success looks like. The outcome we are aiming for is a working prototype, correct?
That is right. By the end of the month, we need a functional demo.
Could you clarify how this fits into the larger project timeline? Is this Phase 1 of a bigger rollout?
Yes. This prototype will determine whether we get funding for the full version.
Let me summarise: a working prototype by month-end, which serves as a proof of concept for the full project. Correct?

name: 确认范围
scenario: the scope of the website redesign
focus: Confirming what is and is not included
chunks: To avoid confusion later, let us define what is in scope and what is not.
So just to confirm, the mobile version is not part of this phase, correct?
If something falls outside the scope, how should we handle it?
I want to be clear on the boundaries before I commit to the timeline.
patterns: To avoid confusion, let us define ___.
If something falls outside ___, how should we ___?
dialogue: Before we proceed, I want to confirm the scope. The mobile version is not part of this phase, correct?
That is correct. Mobile is Phase 2. This phase is desktop only.
Good. If something falls outside the scope, how should we handle it? Do we log it for later or escalate it now?
Log it in the backlog and flag it in the weekly review. That way nothing gets lost.
Perfect. I want to be clear on the boundaries before I commit to the timeline. One more thing: are accessibility features in scope?
Yes, basic accessibility is in scope. We need to meet WCAG standards for the desktop version.

name: 询问优先级
scenario: managing three competing deadlines
chunks: Among these three tasks, which one should I tackle first?
I understand everything is important, but I need to know what is most urgent.
If I can only finish two by Friday, which one can wait until next week?
Help me prioritise so I do not spend time on the wrong thing.
patterns: Among these, which one should I ___ first?
If I can only ___, which ___?
dialogue: Emma, I have three deadlines this week. Among these tasks, which one should I tackle first?
The client presentation is the most urgent. They are expecting it on Thursday.
And the report and the data analysis?
The report can wait until Friday. The data analysis is important but not urgent—next Monday is fine.
So if I can only finish two by Friday, the report can wait. Got it. That really helps me prioritise.

name: 复述交付要求
scenario: confirming the deliverables before starting
chunks: Let me restate what I think the deliverable is, and you tell me if I am off.
So the output should be a five-page report with three data visualisations, right?
Is there a specific format or template I should use?
I want to make sure I build the right thing, not just build things right.
patterns: Let me restate ___.
So the output should be ___, right?
dialogue: So the output should be a five-page report with three data visualisations, right? Let me restate: the report covers Q2 results, compares them to Q1, and includes recommendations.
Almost. It is Q2 versus Q2 of last year, not Q1. And the recommendations should be on a separate page.
Good catch. Is there a specific format or template I should use?
Yes, use the standard quarterly report template. It is in the shared drive.
Got it. I want to make sure I build the right thing. I will use the template and compare Q2 this year to Q2 last year.

name: 汇报已完成
scenario: sharing a weekly status update
chunks: Here is what I have completed this week.
The first phase is done and ready for review.
I finished the data analysis ahead of schedule.
The key achievement this week was resolving the compatibility issue.
patterns: Here is what I have completed: ___.
The key achievement this week was ___.
dialogue: Lin, can you give us a quick status update on the project?
Sure. Here is what I have completed this week. The first phase of the user interface is done and ready for review.
I also finished the data analysis ahead of schedule. The key achievement this week was resolving the compatibility issue that had been blocking the login feature.
Excellent. That was a tricky one. Is anything blocking you now?
Not at the moment. I am on track for the Friday milestone.

name: 说明进行中
scenario: explaining work currently in progress
focus: Describing ongoing tasks and their status
chunks: I am currently working on the user interface. It is about sixty percent done.
The backend integration is in progress, but I have hit a small delay.
I expect to finish the testing phase by Wednesday.
Here is where things stand right now.
patterns: I am currently working on ___. It is about ___ done.
I expect to finish ___ by ___.
dialogue: Where are you on the backend integration?
I am currently working on it. It is about sixty percent done. The API connections are working, but I still need to handle error cases.
I have hit a small delay with the authentication module. The third-party service changed their documentation.
How long will that set us back?
Not much. I expect to finish the testing phase by Wednesday. Here is where things stand: on track for the deadline, but with less buffer than I would like.

name: 提出风险
scenario: flagging a potential schedule risk
focus: Raising concerns before they become problems
chunks: I want to flag a potential risk with the schedule.
If the design review gets delayed, it will push back the entire timeline.
The risk is moderate, but I think we should have a backup plan.
I am not saying it will happen, but I want us to be prepared.
patterns: I want to flag a potential risk: ___.
If ___, it will ___.
dialogue: Emma, I want to flag a potential risk. If the design review gets delayed, it will push back the entire timeline by at least a week.
The risk is moderate. The design team is overloaded, and our review is not their top priority. I am not saying it will happen, but I want us to be prepared.
I think we should have a backup plan: if the review does not happen by Wednesday, I will proceed with an interim design that we can adjust later.
That is sensible. Let us do that.

name: 调整时间线
scenario: renegotiating a deadline after a setback
chunks: Given the unexpected delay, I think we need to adjust the deadline.
I propose moving the delivery date from Friday to next Tuesday.
Here is what I can still deliver by the original date, and what needs more time.
I would rather give you a realistic timeline now than miss a deadline later.
patterns: Given ___, I propose moving the deadline to ___.
Here is what I can deliver by ___, and what needs more time.
dialogue: Given the unexpected delay with the server migration, I propose moving the delivery date from Friday to next Tuesday.
That is disappointing, but I appreciate the honesty. What can you still deliver by Friday?
Here is what I can still deliver: the front-end code is complete and tested. What needs more time is the database integration, which depends on the server being stable.
Okay. I would rather have a realistic timeline now than miss a deadline later. Next Tuesday it is.
Thank you. I will send an updated timeline by the end of the day.

name: 进入议题
scenario: starting a meeting with a clear agenda
chunks: Thanks everyone for joining. Today we have three items to cover.
Let us start with the most urgent item and work our way down.
I suggest we spend fifteen minutes on each topic.
The goal of this meeting is to reach a decision on the vendor.
patterns: Today we have ___ items to cover: ___.
The goal of this meeting is to ___.
dialogue: Thanks everyone for joining. Today we have three items: the vendor decision, the budget update, and next steps for the launch.
Sounds good. How much time do we have?
We have forty-five minutes. I suggest we spend fifteen minutes on each topic. The goal of this meeting is to reach a final decision on the vendor so we can proceed.
Let us start with the vendor then. That is the most urgent.
Agreed. Let us start with the most urgent item and work our way down.

name: 提出建议
scenario: making a suggestion in a team meeting
chunks: I have a suggestion that might save us some time.
What if we tried a different approach to the onboarding process?
One option would be to run a small pilot before rolling it out company-wide.
I would like to propose something based on the data we just reviewed.
patterns: What if we tried ___?
One option would be to ___.
dialogue: I have a suggestion. What if we tried a different approach to the onboarding process? Instead of a full-day session, we could break it into three shorter modules.
That is interesting. What is the benefit?
New hires retain more information in shorter sessions, and it is easier to schedule. One option would be to run a small pilot with the next cohort before rolling it out.
I like that. Low risk, and we would have data to support a wider change.
Let us add that to the agenda for next week. Good suggestion, Mia.

name: 邀请发言
scenario: drawing out quieter team members
chunks: I would like to hear from those who have not spoken yet.
Ben, you have experience with this. What is your take?
Does anyone have a different perspective on this?
Before we move on, any final thoughts from the group?
patterns: I would like to hear from ___.
___, what is your take on ___?
dialogue: I would like to hear from those who have not spoken yet. Ben, you have experience with this kind of migration—what is your take?
Honestly, I think we are underestimating the complexity. The last migration took twice as long as planned.
That is exactly why I wanted to hear from you. Does anyone else have a different perspective?
I agree with Ben, but I think we can mitigate the risk by doing it in stages rather than all at once.
Good. Before we move on, any final thoughts? No? Then let us incorporate Ben's concern and Mia's suggestion into the plan.

name: 总结决定
scenario: summarising what was agreed in a meeting
chunks: Let me summarise what we have decided today.
We agreed on three things: first, the vendor is selected; second, the budget is approved; third, Ben will lead the rollout.
Each action has an owner and a deadline. Please confirm you are clear on yours.
I will send a written summary by the end of the day.
patterns: Let me summarise what we have decided: ___.
Each action has an owner and a deadline: ___.
dialogue: Let me summarise what we have decided today. We agreed on three things: the vendor is selected, the budget is approved at the proposed amount, and Ben will lead the rollout starting next Monday.
That is correct. I will send the rollout plan by Wednesday.
And I will finalise the contract with the vendor by Friday.
Each action has an owner and a deadline. Ben: rollout plan by Wednesday. Mia: contract by Friday. Please confirm you are clear.
I will send a written summary by the end of the day. Thank you, everyone.

name: 肯定具体表现
scenario: giving positive feedback that is specific
chunks: I wanted to let you know that your presentation was excellent.
The way you handled the client questions was particularly impressive.
Your attention to detail on the report saved us from a major error.
That specific contribution made a real difference to the outcome.
patterns: I wanted to let you know that ___.
The way you handled ___ was particularly ___.
dialogue: Lin, I wanted to let you know that your presentation was excellent. The way you handled the client questions was particularly impressive—you stayed calm and gave clear answers even when they pushed back.
Thank you. I was nervous about that part.
It did not show. Your attention to detail on the slides also saved us. The client specifically mentioned how clear the data visualisations were.
I spent extra time on those. I am glad it paid off.
It did. That specific contribution made a real difference. The client signed off on the same day, which almost never happens.

name: 提出改进点
scenario: giving constructive criticism that helps
chunks: I would like to share some feedback that I hope will help you improve.
One area where I think you could grow is meeting facilitation.
This is not about what went wrong—it is about what could be even better next time.
Here is one specific thing I would suggest doing differently.
patterns: I would like to share some feedback on ___.
Here is one specific thing I would suggest: ___.
dialogue: Lin, I would like to share some feedback that I hope will help you. One area where I think you could grow is meeting facilitation.
This is not about what went wrong—it is about what could be even better. In the last three meetings, we ran over time because the discussion went off track.
That is fair. I struggle with keeping things moving when the conversation gets interesting.
Here is one specific suggestion: at the thirty-minute mark, do a quick time check aloud. It signals to everyone that we need to wrap up.
That is actionable. I will try that in the next meeting. Thank you for being direct.

name: 回应反馈
scenario: receiving feedback without defensiveness
chunks: Thank you for sharing that. I appreciate you being direct with me.
That is helpful. Let me think about how I can apply that.
Could you give me a concrete example so I understand better?
I had not noticed that before. I will work on it.
patterns: Thank you for sharing that. ___.
Could you give me a concrete example of ___?
dialogue: Thank you for sharing that feedback. I appreciate you being direct with me.
I was worried it might come across as harsh.
Not at all. That is helpful. Could you give me a concrete example so I understand better? When did I come across as unprepared?
In Tuesday's client call, you seemed to be searching for the Q3 numbers. It made the client question whether we had done our homework.
I had not noticed that before, but you are right. I will make sure I have all key data pulled up before calls from now on.
That sounds like a great plan. I am happy to do a quick pre-call check with you if that helps.

name: 确认修改
scenario: agreeing on specific changes after feedback
chunks: Based on your feedback, here is what I plan to change.
I will revise the introduction to make it more engaging.
Can we check in again in two weeks to see if the change is working?
I want to make sure the adjustment actually addresses your concern.
patterns: Based on your feedback, here is what I will change: ___.
Can we check in again in ___ to see if ___?
dialogue: Based on your feedback, here is what I plan to change. I will revise the introduction of my presentations to be more engaging—less data, more story.
That sounds good. What specifically will you do differently?
I will start with a real customer example instead of a slide full of numbers. Then I will connect the data back to that story.
I like that. Can we check in again in two weeks to see if the change is working?
Yes. I will present the Q4 review in two weeks using the new format, and you can give me feedback afterward.
Perfect. I want to make sure the adjustment actually addresses the concern, not just changes for the sake of changing.

name: 请求资源
scenario: asking for additional help or tools
focus: Making a case for more support
chunks: To meet the deadline, I need one additional developer for two weeks.
Here is why: the testing workload is higher than we estimated.
Without this resource, I think we risk missing the quality bar.
What would it take to get this approved?
patterns: To ___, I need ___. Here is why: ___.
What would it take to get ___?
dialogue: Emma, to meet the Friday deadline, I need one additional developer for two weeks. Here is why: the testing workload is much higher than we estimated.
About forty percent. We found three more edge cases that need automated tests. Without this resource, I think we risk missing the quality bar we promised the client.
I understand. What would it take to get this approved? Is there budget available?
I checked with finance. There is contingency budget for exactly this kind of situation. I just need your sign-off.
Send me the numbers and I will approve it today. Good job flagging this early.

name: 协调分工
scenario: dividing work between two team members
chunks: Let us divide the remaining tasks based on our strengths.
I can take the data analysis if you handle the client presentation.
Does that split feel fair to you?
If you are overloaded, I can take one more item off your plate.
patterns: Let us divide the tasks: I will take ___, and you ___.
Does that split feel fair to you?
dialogue: Let us divide the remaining tasks based on our strengths. I can take the data analysis if you handle the client presentation.
That works. I am more comfortable presenting anyway. What about the documentation?
I can do that too. But that gives me three items and you only one. Does that split feel fair to you?
You are right. Let me take the documentation as well. I will have more time next week.
Perfect. I will do the data analysis and the client presentation. You do the documentation. If you are overloaded later, let me know and I can take one more item.
Deal. Let us check in on Wednesday.

name: 交付说明
scenario: handing off completed work with context
focus: Delivering work so the recipient can act
chunks: Here is the completed report. Let me walk you through the key sections.
The main finding is on page three. I have highlighted it for you.
You will need to update the figures on page seven before the final version.
Let me know if anything is unclear or needs revision.
patterns: Here is the completed ___. The key finding is ___.
You will need to ___ before ___.
dialogue: Ben, here is the completed report. Let me walk you through the key sections.
The main finding is on page three—I have highlighted it. Customer satisfaction is up twelve percent, which is the biggest jump in two years.
Impressive. Anything I need to do before we send it?
Yes. You will need to update the figures on page seven before the final version. The Q4 numbers came in after I finished that section.
Got it. I will update those today. Let me know if anything else is unclear.
Will do. The raw data is in the shared folder if you need it.

name: 会后书面确认
scenario: sending a follow-up email after a meeting
chunks: I am sending a quick summary of what we agreed in today's meeting.
Here are the action items, owners, and deadlines as discussed.
Please reply if anything looks incorrect or missing.
I will follow up on these items by Friday.
patterns: Here is a summary of what we agreed: ___.
Please reply if anything ___.
dialogue: Lin, here is a summary of today's meeting. Action items: Ben handles the vendor contract by Wednesday. Mia updates the budget spreadsheet by Thursday. I will draft the client communication by Friday.
That looks accurate to me. One addition: Ben also agreed to schedule the follow-up meeting for next Monday.
Good catch. I will add that. Please reply if anything else looks incorrect or missing.
Everything else looks right. I will follow up on my action items by the end of the week.
Great. Thanks for the quick turnaround on this.
